# Architecture Decisions

## ADR-1 Spring Boot 4.1.2 on Java 21, generated by Spring Initializr
Latest stable release offered by start.spring.io at generation time (others were SNAPSHOT/RC). Java 21 is the LTS target. Boot 4 starters used: `spring-boot-starter-webmvc`, `-data-jpa`, `-validation`, `-actuator`, `-flyway` plus `flyway-database-postgresql`. Versions come from Boot dependency management.

## ADR-2 Package-by-feature
`university`, `program`, `requirement`, `source`, `tuition`, `country`, `common`. Layer sub-packages exist only where classes exist (no empty packages). No `config` package yet because no custom configuration is needed.

## ADR-3 Flyway owns the schema; Hibernate only validates
`ddl-auto: validate`. Applied migrations are immutable; every change is a new `V<n>__*.sql`. Integrity (unique, FK, CHECK constraints) lives in the database and is tested in `SchemaConstraintsIT`.

## ADR-4 Relational model with provenance
Universities and degree programs are separate. `academic_requirement` and `tuition_fee` are scoped by application cycle / academic year and **must** reference a `source` (`NOT NULL` FK). No facts are seeded; only synthetic test fixtures (ISO codes `XA`/`XB`).

## ADR-5 DTO-only API, whitelisted sorting, stable paging
Entities never reach JSON (records in `dto`, `UniversityMapper`). Sort fields are whitelisted (`name`, `city`) with `id` as tiebreaker; page size 1–100. Country is fetch-joined for list pages to avoid N+1; detail uses an `@EntityGraph`.

## ADR-6 Search via JPA Specifications
Name search is case-insensitive "contains" with `%`/`_` escaped so user input is literal. See mistake #1 for the Spring Data 4 null-spec rule.

## ADR-7 Centralised errors
`GlobalExceptionHandler` returns one `ApiError` shape; framework errors (unknown path, 405) keep their status instead of becoming 500.

## ADR-8 Test strategy
`*Test` = unit/slice tests without Docker (surefire). `*IT` = Testcontainers PostgreSQL 17 (failsafe, run in `verify`). One shared container per JVM.

## ADR-9 Configuration and secrets
Datasource from environment (`DB_URL`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD`), optional git-ignored `.env`. No default password exists anywhere. Compose refuses to start without `DB_PASSWORD`. Default host DB port is 5433 to avoid clashing with native PostgreSQL.

## ADR-10 Program-first model (Milestone 3A)
Programs are first-class: the new `/api/v1/programs` resource returns programs together with the university that offers them. Program-specific facts never move onto the university. Everything new on `degree_program` is nullable (or defaulted) so incomplete but legitimate programs can be imported; unknown stays `NULL`. V2 is purely additive and V1 is untouched. `DegreeLevel` keeps all five values (`DIPLOMA`, `CERTIFICATE` included); bachelor and master are filters like the rest, not special cases.

## ADR-11 Reference data is imported, not migrated
Migrations create structure only. Facts live in `reference-data/programs.json` and are loaded by `ReferenceDataImporter`: validated first, applied in one transaction, idempotent by natural keys, additive (never deletes), and it refuses to overwrite a conflicting tuition figure. It runs only when `IMPORT_REFERENCE_DATA=true`. `ReferenceDataFileTest` guards the shipped file (sources, dates, verification, no placeholder URLs).

## ADR-12 Verification and official application links
`verification_status` + `verified_on` live on the program; each tuition, intake and requirement row cites a `source` whose `retrieved_on` is the date that fact was read. `official_application_url` can only be set for a `VERIFIED` program, enforced by a database CHECK, the entity and the importer, so a client can trust any link the API returns. "Verified" means checked against the cited pages on that date, not a guarantee they stay current.

## ADR-13 Academic fields are rows with a parent
`academic_field(slug, name, parent_id)`. A new subject is a new row. The API filter matches a field and its direct children (two levels). Deeper trees would need a recursive query; not needed yet. The V1 free-text `field_of_study` stays only as a fallback for the university-detail view.

## ADR-14 Stable, globally unique program identifier without a new column
Program slugs are unique per university only. The public identifier is `<university-slug>--<program-slug>`. Slug format forbids `--` (database CHECK, added `NOT VALID` for the program slug so existing rows cannot block the migration), so the split is unambiguous and the identifier is unique by construction. Renaming a slug changes the identifier: treat slugs as permanent.

## ADR-15 Tuition filter semantics
`tuitionMax` needs `tuitionCurrency`; it compares only same-currency, `PER_YEAR` amounts (optionally one applicant category) and excludes programs whose tuition is unknown. Unknown is not "free" and different currencies are never converted or mixed.

## ADR-16 Query efficiency is asserted
List pages fetch university, country and field in the page query and batch the language collection (`@BatchSize`); the detail view loads to-one associations in one entity-graph query and the collections with a fixed number of queries. `ProgramQueryCountIT` fails if statement counts grow with page size. Indexes are kept only if measured as used (V3 dropped `idx_program_name_lower`).

## ADR-17 Institution identity is separate from program facts, and verification has a level below "verified"
V5 adds identity columns and three small tables (external ids, aliases, source links) to `university` and a second importer (`UniversityCatalogueImporter`, `reference-data/universities.json`). Resolution is by stable external id, then slug, then alias in the same country, so a rename or an existing row never produces a duplicate. `verification_status` has three levels: `VERIFIED` (registry match and official site read), `REGISTRY_ONLY` (identity confirmed, site unreadable, no website stored: enforced by a CHECK) and `UNVERIFIED`. It only ever moves up. Alternative rejected: inserting unreadable institutions as verified, or leaving three EU countries empty; either would misstate what is known.

## ADR-18 Monitoring reuses `source`; facts are staged before they are published
`source_monitor` is 1:1 with `source` (no parallel source table); `source_check` is the audit trail; `staged_change` is the staging area with a unique dedupe key. The pipeline is fetch, canonicalise, extract (per-source adapters), normalise, validate, compare, stage, apply-or-review. Only an empty duration or language field read from structured data is published automatically; tuition, deadlines, requirements and any differing value need a person. Dated facts for a new period are new rows; an existing period is never overwritten. Alternative rejected: one generic scraper publishing what it parses; universities do not share markup and a wrong fee is worse than a missing one.

## ADR-19 Crawler boundaries are code, not convention
`UrlGuard` (https only, approved hosts, public addresses, every redirect hop), `RobotsPolicy` (RFC 9309), per-host spacing, a response cap, bounded retries and Retry-After handling live in `PageFetcher`; challenge pages and 401/403 mark a source UNSUPPORTED instead of being worked around. The network is behind `HttpTransport`, so every crawler test uses recorded fixtures. There is no HTTP control surface: registering, crawling, reviewing and re-activating run from the command line (`app.refresh.command`).

## ADR-20 An external scheduler runs unattended checks
The in-process `@Scheduled` runner is off by default. Due-ness (`next_check_at`) is stored in PostgreSQL, so a daily job from any scheduler (platform cron, Cloud Run Job, GitHub Actions) is safe to repeat, delay or restart. Nothing is provisioned without approval.
